<tom>, gather, with the linking ending <in>: {sing tomin} is gathering wood and {bu tomin} is building a nest
<tom>, short, with <kal> in the sense of interval: a short span of time; {tomkal sung} is for a short while
a short time, usually as {tomkha sung}, for a little while; also a short distance, as in {tomkha pai}, go a little farther
<tomkha>, short while, with the diminutive <no>: a very short moment, used with <sung>, within
short but complete; placed after a noun, as in {thu tomkim}, a brief account or summary

<tom>, short, with <lak>, take: a short version of a speech or writing, and as a verb, summarise; {a tomlak in} is in short, abbreviated

<tom>, short, with <lam>: how short something is, said of the length of life

<tom>, short, with <lua>, too much, written as one word: too short in time or length

<tom>, short, and <mahmah>, very, written as one word

<tom> short with the noun suffix <na>: the fact of being short in time

<tom> and <nono> written as one word: short ones, said of several things that are each short
<tom>, short, with the causative <sak>: make shorter, cut short, said of days or of a time of life
<tom> gather firewood with <sak>, do for someone, and the linking ending <in>: gathering wood for another
<tom>, short, with the plural <te>: the short ones; {tangthu tomte} is short stories and {thau tomte} short guns
<tom> and <thei> written as one word: {a tomthei penin} is as briefly as possible

terms: being able to nest/place to nest
definition: <tom>, build a nest, with <theih>, be able, and the noun suffix <na>: {bu a tomtheihna} is that birds are able to nest, said of the branches of a tree
<tom>, short, and <vei>, time, written as one word: a short time; {tomvei sung} is for a short while
<tom>, short, with <zaw>, more: shorter in length, distance or time

the unit of weight, placed before a number or after {metric}, as in {ton khat}, one ton; not {ton} accompany

<tonbucip>, crouch down small, with the linking ending <in>

<tong> cubit with <kua> nine, written as one word

<ton>, draw together in folds, with the linking ending <in>; said of cloth

<tonkhawm>, go together, and <in> written as one word, after <tawh>: going along together with, in company with
<tonkhawm>, go together, with the plural <te>: those who travel along with someone

terms: go together with/accompany/keep in step with

<ton>, draw together in folds, with the noun suffix <na>; {sa tonna} is a wrinkle of the skin
the unit of weight, in the English spelling; also in {10-tonne Lorry}, a ten tonne lorry
have someone with oneself on a journey, take along; the person taken is the object
<tonpih>, take along, with the linking ending <in>
<tonpih>, go with, with <pa> marking a man: the man who is with someone
<tonpih> go with, with plural <te>: the people who are with one on the way
<ton>, accompany, with the causative <sak>: send someone along with others
<ton>, draw in, with the causative <sak>; with <kik>, back, it is draw a stretched-out hand back to the body
<tonsak>, draw in, with <kik> back: bring a stretched-out hand back to the body
Zolai name of Champhai, a town in Mizoram, India, near the border of Myanmar

<Tonzang> with the plural <te>: Tonzang and places like it, or the people of Tonzang

pick up things left lying: of grain, glean; of food, gather up what is left over; {van top} is take plunder

terms: the Lord's favour/the Lord's face/God's grace

<Topa>, the Lord, with the possessive ending {'a}: belonging to the Lord
<to>, upward, and <pah>, at once, written as one word after a verb: the step up is made straight away
<Topa> with the subject marker <in> shortened to {-n}: the Lord as the one who acts, common in blessings

terms: the Lord bless/may the Lord bless

<topa> with the plural <te>; in the verses always in the title Lord of lords

<topaz>, a precious stone, capitalised in the text

make strong and firm, said of the bars of a city gate

<to> dig with <suk>, downward, and the linking ending <in>

<to>, onward, and <ta>, here now or already, written as one word after a verb: the action has gone on and has now come to this point
<to> up with <tai> run; {a suktai a totai kawikawi} is running down and up, here and there
<to>, dig, with <tawm>, by oneself or for oneself: {tuikhuk totawm} is dig cisterns of their own

<to>, dig, with <te>, the people who dig
<to>, lord, with <thum>, three: the three persons of the one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit
<tot>, walk along, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of treading or walking; {a totna mun} is the place where the foot treads, and {lampi totna} is walking in the ways of someone
<to>, upward, said twice and placed after a verb to show that an action or state goes on and increases
<toto>, onward, and the future marker <ding> written as one word; after a verb: will go on doing it, will keep doing it more and more
<toto> and <lai>, here still, written as one word after a verb: the action is still going on and increasing
<toto>, continually, and <laiding>, will still, written as one word after a verb: the action will be carried on further

terms: let us keep on/let us go on

<toto> and <thei> written as one word after a verb: the action can go on further; {ki behlap totothei} is may go on increasing

<tot> with <sa>, already done: describes land or a path on which someone has walked

endure or go on longer than another; from one sentence and a dictionary entry

medical care given to a sick or injured person, used beside {zatui bawl}

the hearing of a case in a court of law

state in the north-east of India

soldiers of an army, mostly written beside or in place of <galkap>

<tua>, that, with <banah>, in addition to, written as one word at the head of a sentence

terms: meanwhile/in the midst of that/while this was so

<tua> and <banga> written as one word: of that kind, in that way, before a noun or a verb

<tua>, that, <bang>, like, and <dan>, manner, written as one word: of that kind, placed before a noun or used alone for such a thing

<tua> and <bangin> written as one word: in the way just described

terms: just like that/in the same way/likewise

<tua> that and <bangte> written as one word: people or things like that
<tuabang>, like that, and <teng>, all, written as one word: all those things, all that has just been told
<tua> and <bek> written as one word: that alone; <tuabek hilo> and <tuabek thamlo> open a sentence as not only that, moreover
<tuabek>, that alone, and <hilo>, is not: opens a sentence, alone or followed by <in>, and adds a further point to what was just said, not only that
<tuabek>, that alone, and <thamlo>, not only: opens a sentence that adds a further fact to what was just said
in that way, as it is: {a tuaci bang} is such a thing, {a tuaci mah} is just like that, and {tuaci omsak} is leave someone or something as it is
<tua> and <ciang> written as one word, mostly followed by <in>: then, when that had happened, the usual way to begin the next step of a report; {tuaciang dong} is up to that point
<tua> and <ciangin> written as one word: after that, then; it opens a sentence that tells what happened next
<tuaci>, in that way, in the form used as a verb: act in the way just spoken of, do so
<tua> and <dan> written as one word: in that way, in that manner; before a noun, that kind of
<tuadan> and <in> written as one word: in that manner
<tua>, that, and <ading>, for, written as one word: for that, for the thing just named
<tua>, that, and <dung>, along, written as one word; {tuadung zui in} is following that, accordingly
<tua> and <dungzui> written as one word, mostly followed by <in>: in keeping with that, accordingly
<tua> and <gam> written as one word: that country, those countries with <te>
<tua>, that, and <gei>, side, written as one word: beside that place, near there
<tua> and <gul> written as one word: that snake, the snake spoken of

short form of <tua-ah>, at that place or in that; the page gives <tua-ah> and {tuah} as the same and counts it among the short forms that need no apostrophe
unit name for two things that meet or are joined: the book gives two <innsun> as {tuah khat}; what exactly is counted is not clear from the page
<tua> and <hang> written as one word, that reason; it begins a sentence, mostly as {tuahang in}, because of that
<tua>, that, and <hangin>, because of, written as one word at the start of a sentence: because of that
<tuahang> and <tawh> written as one word: owing to that, as a result of it
<tuah>, meet with, and <ciangin>, when, written as one word: when one meets with something, mostly trouble

terms: will meet/to be placed/to meet with

<tua>, <hi> and <a> written as one word at the head of a sentence, that being so: therefore
<tua>, that, with <hileh>, if it is, written as one word: if that is so, then; opens a sentence that tells what follows
<tuah>, join or meet, with the linking ending <in>, placed after a verb: {khui tuahin} is sewing together and {kimai tuahin} is face to face
<tuah>, put against, with the linking ending <in>: putting one thing against another so that they touch
<tuah>, meet, with <khak>, happen to: happen to meet a person or meet with an event; {a tuahkhak peuh} is whoever one happens to meet
<tuahkhak>, happen to meet, and <thu>, matter: a thing that has happened to someone, an experience; the one who had it stands before, as in {ka tuahkhak thu}, my experience
<tuahkhak>, meet with, with the noun suffix <na>: what a person has gone through, experience of life
<tuahkhak> and <sa> written as one word: already met with, what one has experienced
<tuah> and <khia> written as one word: carry or move a person or thing out of a place to another, as the sick out of a burning building; {ki tuahkhia} is be moved out or transferred
form of <tuahkhia> used before words such as <in>, <ciangin> and <ding>: carry or move someone or something out of a place, and also get down out of a car
<tuah>, meet with, with <lawh>, as a result: bring upon oneself, come to suffer

terms: if one meets with/when one encounters

<tuah>, meet with, and <ma>, before, written as one word: before meeting with something; {haksatna ka tuahma in} is before I met with hardship
<tuah> come upon, with <mang> away; followed by <sak>, let someone carry off, give as plunder
<tuahmang> with the causative <sak>; let the enemy carry everything off
<tuah>, meet with, with the noun suffix <na>: meeting with or going through something; {na tuahna mun peuh} is any place you happen upon
<tuah> meet with and <pha> good: have good come to one, set against <tuahsiatna>, misfortune
<tuahpha> meet with good, with the causative <sak>
form of <tuahpha> used before <ciangin>
<tuahphat> with the noun ending {-na}: meeting with good, the opposite of misfortune
written after <ki>, the same as <kituahpih>: meet with someone
<tuah> meet with, with <sa> already done; {tuahsa thute} is the things one has gone through
<tuah> meet, come upon, with the causative <sak>; with <mang>, give away as plunder
<tuah> come upon, with the causative <sak> and <mang> away
<tuah> and <sawm>, intend, written as one word: plan to place or settle people somewhere; in headlines {inntungpan tuahsawm} is said of someone who tries to throw herself from a house top
<tuah>, meet with, and <sia>, bad: meeting with misfortune; {mi tuahsia} or {tuahsia mi} is a victim, one struck by trouble
be struck by calamity; {tuahsia-in}, in calamity
of a car, bus, train or other vehicle, have an accident; in headlines also as a noun after the vehicle, <mawtaw tuahsia>, a car accident
form of <tuahsia> used before <ni>, <ciangin> and other following words; {a tuahsiat ni} is the day of their disaster
<tuahsiat>, meet with misfortune, with <ding> written as one word; as {tuahsiatding ciangin}, when misfortune is to come, when an accident is going to happen
<tuahsia> unfortunate with the plural <te>; {mi tuahsiate}, people struck by misfortune

terms: can have an accident/can crash/may come to harm
definition: <tuahsia> and <thei> written as one word: be liable to meet with an accident or misfortune

terms: come to harm by it/fall victim/suffer an accident
definition: <tuahsiat>, meet with disaster, and <lawh>, as a result, written as one word: be hurt or killed as a result of what was named
<tuahsiat>, meet with disaster, with the noun suffix <na>: something bad that befalls a person; {tuahsiatna tuak} is meet with calamity

in news, one sudden event in which a vehicle is wrecked or people are hurt, named after the vehicle as in <mawtaw tuahsiatna>, a road accident, and <vanleng tuahsiatna>, a plane crash; not misfortune in general

<tuahsiatna>, accident, and <aphual>, the very spot: the place where an accident happened, a fixed term of news reports; followed by <ah> or <mahah>, at the scene, on the spot, most often of someone who dies there before help comes
<tuahsiatna>, disaster, with the plural <te>
go down a slope toward a place, the opposite of <kahto>, go up
<tuahsuk>, go down, with the noun suffix <na>: the way down, a slope; {tuahsukna mun} is the place where the road goes down
<tuah>, meet with, with the plural <te>: the things that one meets with or comes upon
reduplicated <tuah>, meet: wherever one comes upon something; {a tuahtuah munah} is right on the spot where they found them
<tuahtuah>, come upon, with the noun suffix <na>: the place where one comes upon something; {a tuahtuahna munah} is on the very spot
<tua>, that, with <hun>, time: at that time; of the past it is followed by <lai-in> or <laitakin>, of the future by <ciangin>

terms: at that very moment/just then/at the time
definition: <tuahun>, at that time, and <laitak>, at the very time: followed by <in>, opens a sentence that tells what was going on at the moment of the event just told
<tuahun>, that time, and <lai>, while, written as one word: at that time in the past, usually followed by <in>

terms: at that very time/at that moment
definition: <tuahun>, that time, and <laitak>, at the very time, written as one word: just at that time, often followed by <in>
<tua> and <hunsung> written as one word: within that time
word of endearment for a small child in lullabies, {ka tuai aw}, my little one; apparently the word for young and tender
poetic word for <nau>, used in songs
the young people of a community, often paired with <khangno> or <khangthak>; a word of the northern Zo dialects used also in Zolai writing
<tuailai>, youth, with the plural <te>
<tua>, that, and the subject marker <in> written as one word; the book names {tua ... in} beside {tua ... pen} as the definite article of Zolai, where the noun stands between the two words
placed after a verb: the action goes on and on without settling, as in {leng tuaituai}, keep flying, and {kisam tuaituai}, be called again and again
be right, fitting or allowed, placed after another verb: {piak tuak} is right to give, and with <lo> it is not allowed
each of them, both alike, placed after a noun, a number or a verb
come upon a person or thing, or meet with an experience such as trouble, fear or punishment
joined to a verb or describing word, it says what the speaker supposes without knowing it: <tawltuak> is must be tired; the book calls it the saying of a supposition, <upmawh>
fall from or into something, as {singkung tungpan tuak}, fall from a tree, and {tui sungah tuak}, fall into the water; the book sets it apart from the supposition
<tuak>, each, with the ending <a>, used after <pang>, side: {pang tuaka om} is being on each side or on both sides

terms: on both sides/on each side/on either side
definition: <tuak>, each or both, with the place marker <ah>, used after <pang> or <lang>, side: on both sides, on each of the two
<tua>, that, and <kawm>, while, written as one word, mostly followed by <in>: while doing that, at the same time as that
placed after a number with its unit: about that much, or as much as that, as in {kum 2 tuakbang}, about two years
<tuak>, meet with, and <ding>, will, written as one word: will meet with or undergo punishment, hardship or the like
<tua> and <khit> written as one word, mostly as {tuakhit ciangin}: after that

terms: soon afterwards/shortly after that/not long after
definition: <tuakhit>, after that, and <asawtlo>, not long: opens a sentence or clause, always followed by <in>, and says that the next event came shortly after the one just told
<tua>, that, with <khit> and <ciang>, after, written as one word: after that, then; also followed by <in>
<tua>, <khit> and <ciangin> written as one word: after that, next
<tua>, that, and <khitzawh>, after, written as one word, mostly at the start of a sentence: after that
<tua> and <khua> written as one word: that town or village, the one just spoken of
<tuak>, meet, with the linking ending <in>: meeting a person, or meeting with death or trouble, and then the next action follows
<tuak>, each, with the ending <in>, mostly after a number: {a nih tuakin} is both of the two; {a tuam tuakin} is each one apart
<tuak> with the linking ending <in>: getting down from an animal or a chariot, or plunging down into something
<tuak>, meet, with <kha>, happen to: come upon a person by chance, find someone doing something, or meet with trouble
<tuak>, meet with, and <khak>, happen to, written as one word: what one happens to meet in life; {tuakkhak thu} is an experience
<tuak>, get down, with <khia>, out: come out and down from a ship or boat
throw oneself down from a high place such as a housetop or a bridge, with <tungpan> before it; not the ordinary getting out of a vehicle
<tuak>, meet with, and <khial>, wrongly: meet with a mishap, make a false step
<tuak>, meet with, and <khin>, already, written as one word: have already met with a loss or a hardship
<tuak> and <kik>, back, written as one word: come out again, said of a patient who can leave the hospital, {zato pan tuakkik}
after <ki>, {ki tuakkik}: <tuak>, meet, and <kik>, again, written as one word, meet each other again
<tuak>, meet with, and <lawh>, as a result: bring something bad upon oneself

terms: if one meets with/when one meets
definition: <tuak>, meet with, and <leh>, if or when, written as one word: if or when someone meets with an accident, hardship or the like
<tuak> meet with and <lo> not, written as one word
<tuak> be fitting with <lo> not, placed after another verb
after <ki>, written apart, the negative of <kituak>: not match or agree with what stands before <tawh>; {ki thu tuaklo} is disagree with one another
<tuak>, each or meet, with the noun suffix <na>; in the text it is part of a section heading, {A Kideih Tuakna}, apparently the desire of each for the other
<tuak>, meet with, and <ngei>, ever, written as one word: have experienced something at some time
<tuak> meet with <pa>, the man: the man who meets or runs into something
<tuak> meet, with <pah> at once
<tuak>, meet, with <peuh>, any: {a tuakpeuh} in the verse is anyone who comes upon him
<tuak>, meet with, and <sak>, cause: make someone meet with or undergo something, usually trouble or punishment
let someone leave a hospital after treatment, often as {ki tuaksak kikpah}, was sent home again at once
move downward from a higher place, also step, climb or jump down, the opposite of <kahto>, go up
<tuaksuk> go down, with the connective ending <in>
<tuaksuk> go down, with <suak> right through

terms: those who meet with/those who suffer
definition: <tuak>, meet with, and the plural <te> written as one word: the people who meet with or suffer something, or the things that are met with; {sihna tuakte} are those who died

terms: things that ought to be done
definition: <tuak>, be fitting, and the plural <te> written as one word after a verb: the things that it is right to do; {sep tuakte} are the things one ought to do

terms: can incur/be liable to/may meet with
definition: <tuak>, meet with, and <thei>, can, written as one word: may meet with or receive something, as a fine or a lawsuit
reduplicated <tuak>, each; said of two who are equally so
<tua>, that, and <kuam> written as one word; in the articles <kuam> is an area or district of a town or country, not only a valley: that area, the area just named
<tua> and <kuamsung> written as one word: that area or district, the surroundings of the place just named
<tua>, that, with <kum>, year, written as one word: that year; {tuakum akipan} is from that year on
<tuak>, each, with the plural ending <un>, after a number: {a nih tuakun} is both of them
<tuak> meet with, with <zaw> more
open enclosed space around or in front of a building: {buk tual} is the courtyard of the tabernacle, {biakinn tual} the court of the temple
in {tual sung mi}, a native-born person as opposed to <peemta> or <khualmi>, a foreigner; also written as one word, <tualsung>
<tual> court, with the ending <a>, of or in
<tua>, that, with <laai>, here a long spelling of <lai> in the sense of place, written as one word and followed by {pan-in}, from: from there, from that place; <tualai> in the lexicon is at that time
<tual> courtyard with the place marker <ah>
after <vanleng> or <meileng>: at the ground where aeroplanes or trains stop, so that {vanleng tualah} is at the airport and {meileng tualah} at the railway station; not the yard of a house
<tua>, that, with <lai>, time, written as one word, often followed by <in>: at the time spoken of
<tualai>, that place or time, and the place marker <ah>: at the place or event just spoken of; it opens a sentence that tells what happened there

<tualai>, here that spot, and <munah>, at the place: at the place just spoken of, there; it opens a sentence or clause and points back to the place of the event told before, and it does not mean at that time or instead of
<tua>, that, and <laimun>, place, written as one word: the place just spoken of

terms: at that very time/just then/at that moment
definition: <tua> and <laitak> written as one word: at the very time just spoken of
<tua>, that, with <lak>, midst, written as one word and followed by <ah> or <panin>: among them, from among them
<tua>, that, and <lakah>, among, written as one word: among them, of those just mentioned
<tua> and <lam> written as one word: that direction or side, there; {tualam ah} is that way, toward it
<tual>, the open communal ground of a village, with <biakna>, worship: the traditional sacrifice of a whole village to ask for rain and a good harvest, and the place where it is held
move about and be busy in a place or an activity, making it one's ground
<tualbial>, be active in a place, with the noun ending {-na}: the place where a person or a group lives and is active
be deep in something or throw oneself into it, a work or a ruin; meaning taken from two sentences only
<tua>, that, with <le>, and, written as one word at the head of a sentence or clause: and with that, then, moreover
<tua> and <leh> written as one word, at the start of a sentence: and, and then, in that case
<tual>, local, with <gal>, war: war inside one country or among one's own people
<tua>, that, with <lian>, exactly, written as one word: just then, at that very point; often as {tualian laitak in}, at that very moment
a village in the Haiciin area in the north of Chin State, Myanmar
society as a whole, made up of the many groups and communities in it; the writer glosses the word with English society, and it is found in two articles of one series only
<tual>, native, with <mi>, person: one who belongs to the place, set against <khualmi>, a stranger; {tualmi nam} is an indigenous people of a country
low in standing or in character, looked down on by others; <tualniam lungsim> is a base mind
<tualniam>, lowly or base, and <lungsim>, mind: a low and uncivil way of thinking and behaving that a people should put away; used with <nei>, have, and <puah>, mend
the state of being low or behind others in standing, knowledge or mind; {lungsim tualniamna} is lowness of mind
<tualniam>, lowly or base, with the plural ending <te>: people of low standing or of base character
<tual> court with <no> small
plural of <tualno>
poetic word, <tual>, open ground of a village, with <nuam>, pleasant: a pleasant dwelling place; in songs and words of mourning it stands for heaven, as in {thangvan tualnuam}, or for a home town
<tua> and <lo> written as one word at the start of a clause: other than that, in addition; {tualo teng} and {tualo te} are the others, the rest

<tualo>, besides that, and <adangzong>, others too: placed at the head of a clause to add something further to what has been said; in news reports it comes before a further number of people, {tualo adangzong mi 3} is three more people besides
large open space of a town where people gather, from <tual>, open space, with <pi>, large
in {puan tualpi}, a long outer garment or robe, also written as one word <puantualpi>
a large level ground laid out for one use, named by the word before it: <kimawlna tualpi> or {bawlung tualpi} is a playing field or football ground, <vanleng tualpi> is an airport
high in standing or level, said of people and of a state of life; the opposite of <tualniam>
a person born in the land, set against <peemta>, a foreigner living there

placed before a noun: belonging to the land and its own people, not brought in from outside; <tualsuak minamte> is indigenous peoples, {tualsuak lai} the native script and {tualsuak party} a local party of the people
<tualsuak>, native-born, and <minamte>, peoples: the indigenous peoples of a country, the fixed term of public life and of the United Nations for them; one such people is {tualsuak minam}
<tualsuak>, native-born, with <mi>, person, written as one word: a person born in the place, and the indigenous people of a land
<tualsuakmi> with the plural <te>: the indigenous people of a land
<tualsuak>, native-born, with the plural <te>: the people born in a place; {Tedim Tualsuakte} is those born and grown up in the town of Tedim
<tual>, the communal ground of a village, with <suang>, stone: the stone at the place of <tualbiakna>, on and under which the offerings are laid
belonging to the home community: {tualsung mi} is a native-born person as opposed to <peemta>, a foreigner living among them
the home community itself as a noun, not a describing word before <mi>: the society people live in together, often set beside <mimal>, the individual

<tualsung>, the home community, and <mite>, people: the people who live in the place that is spoken of, the locals; in news it names the civilians of a town or region, or a local person who is quoted, as in {tualsung mite khatin gen hi}, a local said
plural of <tual>: the courts of a building, mostly of the temple

terms: village priest/keeper of the village ground
definition: the man who keeps the communal ground of a village, as in <tualbiakna>, and leads its rites; the driving out of the spirits before <Khuado> begins at his house

terms: settle in/feel at home/get used to a place
definition: become familiar with a place and its people and at ease there, said of someone living away from home; the meaning is inferred from two sentences
<tual> court, with <teng> all and <ah> in
the killing of people of one's own community or of people who are not enemies in war; of a whole people, massacre or genocide
one who kills a person of his own community, a murderer; also the act itself; often paired with <mithat>
<tual>, local ground, with <vak>, walk about: going about from place to place, said of people who offer a service in the villages
spread over something so that it is hidden, or wrap it round, as cloud covers a mountain or a cloth covers the face
separate from the others or different from them: {a tuam} is separately, {tuam om} is live apart, {nu tuam} is of a different mother

terms: all the more/the more for it
definition: placed after a verb or describing word: more so as a result of what was just said, as in {dam tuam}, be the healthier for it, and {ol tuam}, be the easier for it; not the {tuam} of being different

<tuam>, separate, with the expressive word <vilvel>, which strengthens it: wholly apart from the rest, in a special way of its own; used as {a tuam vilvel in} or {a tuam vilvel a} before a verb, or as {a tuam vilvel} before a noun
<tuam.2>, separate, with <vilvel-in> written as two words: after <a>, as {a tuam vilvel in}, apart from the rest, as a separate or special matter; stands before the verb
<tua> and <ma> written as one word, mostly followed by <in>: before that, up to then
<tuam>, separate, with the ending <a>, written as one word and mostly after <a>: {a tuama}, separately, apart from the rest
<tua> that with the emphatic <mah>; {tuamah bangin}, in the same way, likewise
apparently <tuam> separate with the place marker <ah>: in the separate place, his own place
<tuamah> and <bangin> written as one word, at the start of a sentence: in that same way, likewise
<tua> and the first part of <manin> written as one word, with <in> written apart: because of that; it begins a sentence that gives the result
<tua> and <manin> written as one word at the head of a sentence: because of that, therefore
<tuam>, different or separate, and <bawl>, make, written as one word: treat a person differently from others, or make a thing as a separate one
the treating of a person or a group differently from others and not as equals
<tuam>, different, with <ciat>, each, written as one word: different for each one, each having its own
<tuam>, cover, with <cip>, tightly: cover over completely or wrap all round, said of smoke, darkness, worms, shame or love
<tuamcip> cover completely with the linking ending <in>
<tuamcip> wrap up completely, with <pa>, the male one who does it
of another kind, not the same as before or as the rest; placed after the noun
<tuam>, different, and <diak>, especially, written as one word: out of the ordinary, unlike the usual; with <in> it is an adverb, in a special way
<tuam>, cover or wrap, and <ding>, written as one word: must cover, is to be wrapped

terms: will all the more/will be the better for it
definition: <tuam>, here placed after a verb for the more so as a result, and <ding>, will, written as one word: will do or be so all the more because of what was said before
<tua> that, with <mi> person
<tuam>, cover, with the linking ending <in>: covering something, and then the next action follows
<tuam>, separate, with the ending <in>: {a tuamin om} is be separate, {a tuamin koih} is put apart, {a tuamin pai} is go by themselves
somewhat different from the others or from what is usual; built on <tuam>, different
<tuam>, wrap or cover, with <kep>, keep: keep something wrapped up with care, and so protect and cherish a person
<tuam> separate, different, with <khat> one; of another kind, here of a hidden meaning
<tuam> cover with <kik> again
<tuam>, separate, with <koih>, put: keep apart from the rest for a special use, for a person or for God
<tuamkoih> set apart, with <lam>, the fact or manner of doing it
<tuamkoih> set apart, with <pa>, the man who is so
<tuamkoih> set apart with <sa>, already done

terms: set aside in turn/pass on a share
definition: <tuamkoih> set apart, with <sawn> pass on to the next
<tuam> and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: not in particular, not any the more, as in {om tuamlo}, there is none in particular; compare <tuan>
<tuam>, cover, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not cover, said of a woman who does not cover her head
<tuam> apart, with <lup> lie down; the opposite of <lupkhawm>, lie together
a thing that covers or wraps, as the coverings of the tent or a band over the eyes
in {nop tuamna}, a special joy given as a reward
in {phat tuamna}, the spaced spelling of <phattuamna>: the good or gain that comes from something, as {mipiphat tuamna}, the public benefit; not a covering
<tuam> and <pah> written as one word after a verb or describing word: the state comes about markedly and at once, as in {nuam tuampah}, become all the more pleasant
<tuam> different, with the intensifying <pi>
of another kind or appearance than the rest, unlike the usual: {a tuampian mun} is a spot on the skin that looks different
<tuam> cover with <sa>, already done, and the ending <in>: with the head covered
wrap or cover something for someone, as bandaging a wound or a broken arm, or covering the eyes

after a describing word, <tuam> in its meaning all the more with the causative <sak>: make something the better, the easier or the less as a result, as in {nop tuamsak}, ease, and {kiam tuamsak}, reduce; not wrapping or covering
<tuamsak> bind up with the linking ending <in>
<tuam> apart, with <sap> call
in {teel tuamte}: <teel> choose with <tuam> apart and the plural <te>, those specially chosen
in {sin tuamte}: what covers the liver, the lobe of the liver, with the plural <te>
<tuam> different with the plural <te>, outside the fixed {teel tuamte} and {sin tuamte}: after a noun as {tuam tuamte} it is the various kinds of it, and {a om tuamte} is those who stay apart
<tuam> and <tek> written as one word: each one different, each its own
<tuam> apart, with <ton> go together and the connective ending <in>
<tuam> separate, with <tuak> each; each by itself
reduplicated <tuam>, different: of various kinds, placed after a noun, as in {nam tuamtuam}, different kinds, and {gam tuamtuam}, the various provinces
<tuamtuam> with the marker <a>: in the various, as in {gam tuamtuama om}, living in the various provinces
<tuamtuam>, various, with the place marker <ah>: in various, as in {mun tuamtuamah}, in various places
<tuamtuam>, various, with the ending <in>: {a lam tuamtuamin} is in various ways, {a nam tuamtuamin} in all kinds of ways
<tuamtuam> and <pan> written as one word after a noun: from various ones, as {media tuamtuampan}, from various media
<tuamtuam> and <tawh> written as one word: with, by or because of various things of the kind named before it
plural of <tuamtuam>, placed after a noun: things of various kinds, as {kung tuamtuamte}, plants of every kind
plural of <tuamtuam>: the different ones, as {minam tuamtuamte}, the different peoples, and {beh tuamtuamte}, the various clans
<tuamtuam>, various, and <ten>, the plural marker of the doer, written as one word after a noun: the various ones, as the doer of the action
<tuamtuam> various and <zong> also, written as one word after a noun: different kinds of it as well
<tua> and <mun> written as one word: that place, the place just spoken of
<tua>, that, and <munsan>, exact place, written as one word
placed after a verb, mostly before a negative or in a question: even so, in spite of that, any more than others
form of <tuang>, ride, used before <na> and <nading>: {tuan’na} is the animal that one rides, a mount
step heavily on something and crush it under the feet; also treat people cruelly, defeat enemies completely
<tuancil>, trample, with <gawp>, violently: trample down thoroughly and ruin
<tuancil>, trample, with the linking ending <in>: trampling on someone, and then the next action follows
<tuancil> trample with <sak> cause or allow: let someone trample on another
<tuancil> trample with the plural <te>: those who trample on someone
said of a plague that goes beyond the usual, especially severe
<tuan>, ride, and <ding> written as one word: going to ride in a vehicle, in order to travel by car, bus, train or plane
the particle <tuan>, even so, and <ding> written as one word at the end of a question: what would there be then, would it be any different
ride on an animal or in a chariot, or get on it to ride, usually with <tungah>, on
<tuang> ride, with the connective <a>; riding and then
attack by trampling or striking, with <gawp> violently
<tuang> and <ding> written as one word: will ride, going to travel by a vehicle; before a noun, who is about to board
part of the traditional house named with the veranda and the shelves, apparently the planked floor or raised platform of the main room; also the name of a village, written {Tuangdung}
<tuang>, ride or travel aboard, with the linking ending <in>: riding a horse, a donkey or a chariot, or sailing on a ship
<tuang> and <khawm> written as one word: ride on the same vehicle, boat or animal together
poetic word for the road or the path one follows, used in songs and poems, also of the course of a life
<tuang>, ride, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not get on or travel in a vehicle, a boat or on a horse
<tuang>, ride, with <pa>, the male one: he who rides, the rider of a horse

terms: board at once/get in at once
definition: <tuang> ride, board, with <pah> at once and the connective ending <in>
<tuang> ride with <sa>, already done, and the ending <in>: being mounted on an animal
<tuang>, ride, with <sak>, cause: put someone on an animal or in a chariot to ride
put a picture or a text on something for people to see: a portrait on money after <tungah>, a picture on a web page, or words on Twitter after <ah>; nobody rides
<tuangsak> with the linking ending <in>: putting someone on an animal or into a boat, and then the next action follows
<tuang>, ride, and <saklo>, not let, written as one word: not allow someone to board a train or a plane
<tuang> and <suak> written as one word: ride right through or go on riding without getting off
<tuang> ride, with <suk> downward
<tuang>, ride, with the plural <te>: those who ride, as in {sakol tuangte}, horsemen
<tuang>, ride, and <thei>, able, written as one word: be able to ride in a vehicle, or of a vehicle, be able to carry so many people

terms: will be able to ride/can ride
definition: <tuang> and <theiding> written as one word: will be able to ride, and of a vehicle, so many people can ride in it

terms: ride up/go up by vehicle/travel up
definition: <tuang>, ride, and <to>, up or onward, written as one word: go up or onward riding in a train, car or lift
<tua>, that, with <ni>, day: the day just spoken of
<tua>, that, with <ni>, day, written as one word and with a capital at the start of a sentence; {Tuani bekin}, only on that day
<tua> and <nitak> written as one word: on the evening or night just spoken of
<tuan>, form of <tuang>, ride, and <kawm>, while, written as one word, usually followed by <in>: while riding on a motorcycle, in a car or on a train
<tuan> and the negative <kei>, written as one word after a verb: not so in spite of what was done or said, still not, not any the more

tread on something with the foot and crush it
<tuankham>, trample, with the linking ending <in>: trampling something underfoot before the next action
<tuan>, form of <tuang>, ride, with <khop>, together, written as one word: ride in the same vehicle with someone
